correctness.rationale: For a retract H=e(L), idempotence gives H∩[L,L]=e([L,L])=[H,H]. The image of the quotient projection is therefore the abelianization of H, not just a quotient of it. By induction down the lower central series, a subalgebra surjecting onto the abelianization generates the entire nilpotent algebra. Quotient ranks 0, 1, 2 thus force the zero map, a one-dimensional image (alternation, including in characteristic two), and the identity, respectively. For a fixed rank-one quotient projection P onto U along W, fix a nonzero v in U and its normalized functional λ with kernel W. Every lift is x↦λ(πx)u with πu=v, and all q^(n−2) such maps are Lie homomorphisms and idempotent. A commuting quotient projection preserves both lines U,W and is either P or I−P. With usual composition, distinct same-fiber lifts satisfy ef=e and fe=f; complementary fibers instead give ef=fe=0. Pairing the q(q+1) quotient projections by complement gives the claimed disjoint complete bipartite components. With M=2mb nontrivial vertices, the commuting ordered pairs are M+2 diagonals, 2mb² ordered proper edges, and 4M+2 other ordered pairs involving 0 or 1, hence M(b+5)+4. The rank and clique polynomials, maximal families, limit and graph reconstruction follow. The two five-dimensional examples have lower-central classes 3 and 4 and the same q,n. The generator-image checker was read, not executed; its prime-field examples cannot justify general fields, which the characteristic-independent proof covers.

evidence: The free class-two result handles arbitrary generator rank within that class, and the same-day free nilpotent result treats higher classes in the free family. The 1997 abstract characterizes retracts of finitely generated free Lie algebras; accessible material did not specify an arbitrary finite-dimensional nilpotent quotient graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Higher numbers of generators in a free class-two theorem are not stronger at the present class and quotient scope. A rank classification in free higher-class algebras is also not an arbitrary quotient theorem. Full-text priority risk for the 1997 article remains.

evidence: The group theorem uses the Frattini quotient of an exponent-p group; direct Lazard transfer cannot supply the Lie theorem in unrestricted class, especially at class at least p. The free-family hypotheses exclude nonfree examples such as the class-four filiform example.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Similar proof moves and special-case consequences are not implication over all hypotheses. The class-independent lift/commutation result and the resulting blindness across different nilpotency classes are the assessed residue, not the Heisenberg count or graph shape in isolation.

evidence: The exponent-p group paper for Frattini dimension 2 splits into p(p+1)/2 copies of K_(p^c,p^c) for |G′|=p^c, with an analogous quotient-projection mechanism. The exterior algebra has q(q+1)/2 copies of K_(q,q) for unital multiplicative maps.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In group Frattini dimension 2 all proper nontrivial retractions do have cyclic order-p image, so comparing to the full graph, not merely the named cyclic subgraph, is appropriate. Neither the exponent-p group theorem nor the exterior associative theorem has equivalent hypotheses to the frozen Lie claim.
searches: DOI 10.1080/00927879708826054 retracts of free Lie algebras

evidence: At r=2 the free class-two clique count gives exactly q³(q+1)/2 maximal families, and the free two-step rank result gives 1+q²(q+1)T+T³. The associative and exponent-p group graph formulas match as numerical families after parameter alignment.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The three-dimensional Heisenberg instance and analogous graph formulas are credited as exact overlaps. The inspected formulas are not a census for arbitrary Lie brackets and dimensions with two generators.

originality.rationale: The graph shape and quotient-lifting idea have clear precedents. The supported distinct claim is the entire ordinary Lie graph for arbitrary finite-dimensional two-generated nilpotent Lie algebras, at all prime powers including characteristic two and beyond the class range of the standard Lazard correspondence; no inspected precedent has that scope.
residual_risks: Equivalent retraction statements could occur under Frattini quotients or semidirect splittings in uninspected literature.
The 1997 free Lie retract paper could not be assessed beyond its abstract. The related same-day records establish partial coverage but not within-day priority.

value.rationale: This classifies a natural incidence invariant for a whole class of algebras, not just a rank list or another example. It identifies exactly which pairs commute, how many lifts follow each abelianized projection, and exactly what the graph can recover (field size and dimension but not class), hence shows independence from arbitrary higher bracket relations. The special-case counts and analogy alone are not credited as value.
